questions.q: What are the four dimensions the CMDB Health Dashboard scores?
options: Completeness, Correctness, Compliance, and duplicate rate
Speed, Uptime, Cost, and Security
Discovery, Import, Manual entry, and API
Server, Network, Application, and Database CI classes only
questions.explain: These four dimensions give a CMDB a measurable, trendable health score instead of a subjective impression.

questions.q: What does the Completeness dimension specifically measure?
options: Whether required fields on a CI are actually populated
Whether a CI has ever been discovered by Discovery
How many relationships a CI has to other CIs
How old a CI record is
questions.explain: A CI can exist in the table and still be practically useless if fields like Operational Status or Support Group are blank.

questions.q: How is Correctness different from Completeness?
options: Correctness checks whether populated data actually passes validation and makes sense, while Completeness just checks whether fields have any value
They measure exactly the same thing under two names
Correctness only applies to relationships, not field values
Completeness is scored only once, while Correctness is continuous
questions.explain: A field can be populated (Complete) with a nonsensical value, like a CPU count of zero, which Correctness is designed to catch.

questions.q: Why does a dashboard score matter more than a one-time audit?
options: It can be trended over time and drilled into down to specific fields and records, turning into an actionable remediation backlog
A dashboard score is purely cosmetic and has no drill-down capability
One-time audits are always more accurate than ongoing scores
Dashboards replace the need for any Identification or Reconciliation rules
questions.explain: The real value is the drill-down and trend line, which turn a vague impression into a bounded, trackable cleanup task.

questions.q: What does the Compliance dimension depend on, per this lesson?
options: Alignment with the outcomes of Identification and Reconciliation rules
Whether the CI was created by Discovery rather than manual entry
The number of incidents logged against the CI
Whether the CI belongs to the hardware CI class
questions.explain: Compliance reflects whether a CI's data lines up with what Identification and Reconciliation rules, covered in the next lesson, expect.
